definition: q_i^* = sqrt(sum_j (s_j*r_ij)^2/N), where stored finite S_inv components s_j and residual components r_ij are interpreted as exact reals. This does not substitute the real reciprocal of an independently defined ideal S.

assumptions: Native CPU FP64 weighted element multiplication and p=2 norm follows nonnegative rounded square/add/sqrt path, with no more than K64=4N+32 effective FP64 rounding operations along an input-to-output path; FMA/reassociation are permitted only if separately shown to satisfy this bound.

FP32 scalar cast, sqrt(N), and final division collectively admit standard relative gamma_16 with round-to-nearest; N converts exactly, and std::sqrt(float) plus item<float> respect the assumed error model.

All operands and intermediates are finite without overflow; all underflow, subnormal, flush-to-zero and non-relative effects on final RMS are independently bounded in absolute value by 1e-30 per endpoint. This allowance is an explicit hypothesis, not verified by a captured per-element range.
Same stored S_inv and identity H at both endpoints; no extra change in weights or context.
conditional_derivation.logic: Write g64=K64*u64/(1-K64*u64), g32=K32*u32/(1-K32*u32). Conditional on the above, q_native / q_exact lies between (1-g32)*sqrt(1-g64) and (1+g32)*sqrt(1+g64), before absolute underflow allowance. For 0<g64<1, sqrt(1-g64)>=1-g64, so an intentionally looser rational factor f=1/((1-g32)*(1-g64))-1 bounds both sides. Then nu_i <= q_native_i*f + 1e-30.

interpretation: Conditional bound is substantially smaller than observed native RMS gap 0.0019075383808737633 and can be subtracted from the remaining budget.
